meta.title: Sortable
meta.description: A headless drag-to-reorder system. Wrap any list in SortableRoot, mark rows with SortableItem, and optionally restrict drag to a SortableHandle grip. useSortableList manages the item array.

blocks.content: The engineering problem isn't dragging. The browser's pointer events are well-understood, and dnd-kit handles them correctly — including touch, mobile, and high-DPI screens. The engineering problem is architecture: making drag work on the whole row or only a grip handle, rendering a ghost that follows the cursor while items rearrange, and giving the consumer clean state primitives without coupling them to dnd-kit internals.

SortableRoot sets up the DndContext and handles the drag lifecycle — start, move, end, cancel. SortableItem registers each row as a sortable target and applies the displacement transform. SortableHandle carries dnd-kit's event listeners down via React context, so only the grip triggers drag when handle mode is on. useSortableList manages the item array with insert, remove, update, and keyboard move.

blocks.title: Overlay is optional
blocks.content: Without renderOverlay, dnd-kit lifts the item's own DOM node. The dragged element shifts in place and the list reorders around it. Pass renderOverlay to SortableRoot for a ghost card that follows the cursor while the original stays faded at its source position.
Drag any row to reorder. The second list uses handle-only mode — only the grip icon triggers drag.

blocks.label: Interactive demo

blocks.content: The simplest setup. Every row is draggable — no grip needed. Pass items (any array with id: string), and onReorder receives the full reordered array after each drop. Pass setItems from useSortableList directly.

blocks.title: id is the only requirement
blocks.content: T extends { id: string }. Everything else is yours. The engine doesn't care about shape — it only tracks ids to compute the new order.

Add the handle prop to SortableItem and place SortableHandle anywhere inside. Only the grip icon triggers drag — the rest of the row behaves normally. Buttons, inputs, and links inside the row remain fully interactive.

blocks.title: Custom handle appearance
blocks.content: SortableHandle renders a grip icon by default. Pass children to replace it with any element — an icon, a drag affordance, or a fully custom button. The drag listeners are applied to whatever you pass.

renderOverlay receives the active item and renders inside a DragOverlay portal, positioned above all content. The original SortableItem fades to 40% opacity while the overlay follows the cursor. Use this to give dragging a distinct, elevated feel.

blocks.content: The overlay renders in a portal — it's not inside SortableRoot's DOM subtree. Any SortableHandle inside renderOverlay is visual only; it won't receive drag listeners in the overlay context.

useSortableList manages the item array with typed mutations. Pass setItems directly as the onReorder prop — it matches the (items: T[]) => void signature exactly. Use insert, remove, update, and move for programmatic changes outside of drag.
